summary: Calendar gains first_free_slot(minutes, day_start, day_end), which returns the first free stretch of at least N minutes inside the working day.
Why: a scheduler could list gaps but not ask for a free slot of a given length. gaps also leaks outside the window when a booking lies outside it.
Callers get a Slot, or Calendar::NoFreeSlot ("no free slot of 60 minutes in 09:00-17:00") when nothing fits.

blocks.title: How first_free_slot picks a slot
blocks.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  A[gaps day_start, day_end] --> B[clamp gap to day]
  B --> C{empty after clamp?}
  C -- yes --> A
  C -- no --> D{length >= N minutes?}
  D -- yes --> E[return Slot]
  D -- no --> A
  A -- none left --> F[raise NoFreeSlot]

focus.title: Clamping works around a gaps quirk
focus.detail: gaps returns ranges outside the window when a booking lies outside it. first_free_slot clamps to the window; gaps itself is unchanged and is worth its own work item.

focus.title: Raises instead of returning nil
focus.detail: New Calendar::NoFreeSlot, matching the Conflict pattern, so a missing slot cannot be passed on to book.
